additions: Decline speed is itself evidence: the portal timestamp (16:20:10, US Eastern inferred from verified_at_utc 20:21Z) and the 07:25 UTC audit commit bound the RNAAS decision to ≤ ~11 hours after submission, with 'scientific_editor: Not Assigned' — this is a moderator (appropriateness/format) decline, not a refereed rejection. Plan for that gate: the moderator reads the abstract and first paragraph against a 'does this communicate a result?' test.

No CTOI has ever been promoted to TOI without a SPOC or QLP TCE behind it (Guerrero et al. 2021: 'All CTOIs which have been promoted to TOIs were also TCEs in the SPOC pipeline or the QLP'; 106 of 169 came from triage mistakes). For TESS-field candidates, query the MAST TCE/TEV lists first; a signal with no TCE needs a manual reprocessing step that the TOI team rarely performs.

The ExoFOP Community Candidates list (view_ctoi.php) contains 5,138 rows, every one with Discovery Data Source = TESS, so as of 2026-10-17 the Kepler/K2/'beyond' path announced on 2026-08-19 has zero precedent; expect to be the first and to need exofop-support@ipac.caltech.edu guidance on the TID.nn naming for a Kepler-source candidate.

NEA's K2 candidate table shows no candidate-only ingestion with disc_year > 2022 (last: Zink et al. 2021, 152 rows; Zink et al. 2019 RNAAS, 16 rows). Treat 'RNAAS candidate catalog gets into NEA' as a closed historical path; only confirmed planets (accepted peer-reviewed papers) have entered k2pandc since.

MNRAS is fully open access since January 2024 (RAS announcement), so OUP's Low- and Middle-Income-Countries APC policy is the relevant one; India's national ONOS page says OUP applies a 25% APC discount automatically for India-based corresponding authors of fully-OA journals. Also Read-and-Publish agreements cover the APC entirely if the corresponding author's primary affiliation is a participating institution — a concrete reason to let a professional co-author at such an institution be corresponding author.

AAS quanta exclude authors, affiliations, acknowledgements and references, so a methods-heavy AJ paper with a long bibliography is cheaper than a naive word count suggests; and the AAS Publication Support Fund (journals.aas.org/support) covers AJ/ApJ/ApJS/ApJL, is requested during submission, prioritises authors with no funding, is decided by the Editor in Chief, and 'does not guarantee' an award.

Zenodo record type and packaging matter for discoverability: Kuber's record is type 'Software' (GitHub-integration zip, 118 MB, 23 views, 1 download) with no standalone PDF; Rabtsevich split a 'Preprint' record with a 117 KB manuscript.pdf (6,978 views, 912 downloads) from a 'Dataset' record (968 views). Deposit the note as a Preprint record plus a separate Dataset record and cross-link them.

Planet Hunters TESS leadership has changed: the team page states 'Now Nora has left the project' and Ian Mason (a volunteer, lead author of the Oct-2026 RNAAS) now uploads sectors; PHT policy routes credit/authorship discussions through contact@zooniverse.org and requires citing Eisner et al. The Mason note shows the current PHT template: RNAAS (received/accepted Sept, published 6 Oct) → CTOI with paper URL two days later; the note says PHT has registered 'over 190' CTOIs (182 under 'eisner' + 9 under 'mason' = 191 in the CSV).

AI-disclosure requirements differ by venue and must all be satisfied on a single manuscript: AAS = disclose at submission AND an end-of-article statement (GAIDeT template offered; figure captions must name the tool); MNRAS = disclose in the cover letter AND in Methods/Acknowledgements; PASP/IOP = model/version/use in Acknowledgements; arXiv = report significant generative-AI use. AAS explicitly says the guidelines 'concern the manuscript, not the data analysis', so describe agent-run analysis in Methods as methodology, not only in the AI statement.

The ExoFOP TOI FAQ (tess.mit.edu/toi-releases/toi-release-faqs/) still tells readers 'If you find a planet candidate submit it to ExoFOP-TESS'; it is stale relative to the 2026-08-19 ExoFOP rule — cite ExoFOP's own pages, not the FAQ, in any plan or README.

Prior-search diligence beyond catalogues: eumemic's pipeline greps arXiv astro-ph.EP abstracts for TESS/TOI/TIC mentions, and Kuber's miss (Barber et al. 2022 Table 5, Kepler flag Y) came from a membership catalogue. Before any novelty wording, search by exact Gaia DR3 ID in VizieR/CDS tables, ADS full text, arXiv, and the NEA TCE tables, and email the authors of any hit.

Reputational pattern visible in the HN thread (120 comments): beyond the LLM-prose irritation, a commenter alleged 'the author lies about using AI for the writeup in the comments' — inconsistency between stated and visible AI use draws more hostility than disclosed use. Disclose once, prominently, and identically everywhere.

TESS DDT practicalities: Sector 110 begins 2026-10-31 (DDT #100's window); the DDT page allows late submissions 'up to two weeks before sector start ... under certain circumstances'; the template only asks for 'Proposer #1 (Institution | email)' and is reviewed by the TESS PI plus one expert, so an independent researcher can propose. Only worthwhile if your signal is TESS-detectable (not the case for a G=16.3 Kepler-field star).
